stem:
For which of the following reasons are young children and infants more predisposed to the development of respiratory failure than adults? Choose one option.

A. Smaller diameter airways
B. Relatively reduced immunity
C. Increased susceptibility to ventilation–perfusion mismatch
D. Increased foetal haemoglobin
E. Inefficient respiratory muscles
explanation: Infants and young children are more vulnerable to respiratory failure because they have smaller airways, relatively reduced immunity, and a greater tendency to ventilation–perfusion mismatch. Increased foetal haemoglobin is not a typical reason for respiratory failure risk.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: Pediatric respiratory failure risk is increased by anatomical and physiological differences: smaller airways, less effective immune defenses, higher susceptibility to V/Q mismatch, and weaker/less efficient respiratory muscles. The option including A, B, and C is the best available answer.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because it omits smaller airways and reduced immunity, which are important contributors.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: smaller airways, reduced immunity, and V/Q mismatch all increase the risk of respiratory failure in children.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because increased foetal haemoglobin is not one of the main reasons listed.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because it includes foetal haemoglobin and omits inefficient respiratory muscles.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because increased foetal haemoglobin is not a standard reason for increased susceptibility.
